purpose.primary: A single corrective primary contrast: the canonical diagonal in a pre-specified basis, evaluated on fresh data. Competitor-family testing retains its other historical comparators.
purpose.only_admissible_headline: on this registered cohort, the full predictor has lower aggregate empirical-TV loss than the diagonal rule in the pre-specified constant-first, emitted-order basis, exceeding the registered margin on both maps.
purpose.headline_gate: Only a validated cross-term joint PASS permits this headline; identify the v25 cohort and margin 1/240. Competitor-family outcomes are reported separately, without broadening this claim.
purpose.orientation_recommendation: No oracle-selected, training-selected or optimized orientation comparator. A prospectively fixed random-orientation report is descriptive only, outside every inference family and verdict.
purpose.known_quantifier_boundary: For ideal orthonormal B and a=normalized B^T sqrt(p), choose one axis of BR parallel to a. Then the diagonal rule equals the ideal full predictor. Thus superiority over all orientations, intrinsic necessity of cross terms, and basis-independent necessity are impossible claims here. This mathematical inclusion is not an empirical endpoint.

proof: Within a campaign, equality of two identity seeds implies 1000*(k-k_prime)=o_prime-o with o,o_prime in {0} union [50000,50023].

If offsets are both zero or both path offsets, the right side has absolute value <=23, so equality forces k=k_prime and o=o_prime. If one offset is zero, the right side has absolute value >=50000 whereas 1000*abs(k-k_prime)<=19000; equality is impossible.

Cross-term identities lie in [1000000001000,1000000070023]; competitor identities lie in [2000000001000,2000000070023]; the intervals are disjoint. Each campaign has 20*25=500 distinct numeric identities; together 1000.
The largest identity is 2000000070023 < 2^53 < 2^64. All acquisition seed additions are nonwrapping integers, and any binary64 conversion of these integers is exact.

Documented historical registered acquisition bases are at most 910000; s and s+50000+j are therefore at most 960023, below the new identity intervals. This arithmetic statement concerns those documented registered paths.

canonical_diagonal.input: n ordered states; finite binary64 emitted vectors u_1,...,u_m in literal emitted order; the preparation and scored data do not choose this basis
canonical_diagonal.exact_input: Decode every finite binary64 entry as its exact dyadic rational. Reject non-finite entries. Do not substitute archived SVD left vectors for emitted vectors.
canonical_diagonal.arithmetic: Exact rational unnormalized Gram-Schmidt; positive square roots represented by certified rational isolating intervals; correctly rounded binary64 output. No BLAS, SVD or QR routine selects directions or signs.

spectral_cutoff.H: H = (1/n) 11^T + sum_j u_j u_j^T, an exact rational symmetric matrix
spectral_cutoff.lambda_max: largest real eigenvalue of H; exact algebraic comparison using a characteristic polynomial and certified root isolation; trace(H)/n <= lambda_max <= trace(H) is an allowed early decision bound
spectral_cutoff.meaning: constant-preserving ordered numerical dependence rule using the inherited theoretical binary64 cutoff scale; it is not asserted to equal SVD rank truncation
spectral_cutoff.boundary: keep only when d_j > tau_squared; exact equality is discarded. An undecided root comparison is numerical-unresolved, never silently treated as dependence.

algorithm: Set v_0 = 1, d_0 = n, e_0 = v_0/sqrt(d_0), with its positive entries. Keep this direction unconditionally.
For each emitted u_j, compute v = u_j - sum_(h previously kept) v_h (v_h^T u_j)/d_h, exactly; d = v^T v.
If d <= tau_squared, record the column as numerically dependent and continue. Otherwise append v, d and e = v/sqrt(d), with the positive root. Never pivot or reorder columns.
The sign convention is e^T u_j = sqrt(d)>0. This preserves the emitted orientation. No maximal-component-positive sign flip is applied.
Serialize retained/discarded source-column indices, rational directions/norms, cutoff/root certificates, rounded basis, rank and control results.

rounding.rounding: IEEE binary64 nearest, ties to even; certify one rounding cell per entry; rational/algebraic equality handles an exact midpoint
rounding.unresolved: Do not emit an arbitrary rounded value; mark the endpoint numerical-unresolved.

canonical_diagonal.rank_two_identity: With one emitted vector u, w=u-(sum_i u_i/n)1 and s=w^T w>tau_squared, the returned basis is exactly (1/sqrt(n), w/sqrt(s)) = (e_0,e_1). The centering/sign convention is the paper carrier convention.

span_control.rank: require canonical rank equals the unchanged admitted numerical rank

span_control.q_full_preservation: Do not replace the legacy q_full or leverage/linear laws. For mathematical common-span statements use the exact canonical full law; certify its TV distance from the unchanged floating full law at most 1e-10. If not certified, affected v25 endpoints are unresolved.
span_control.failure: retain the unit and mask; no new exclusion, seed substitution or alternative basis is permitted

canonical_diagonal.probability_law: Let B contain the canonical orthonormal columns, x=sqrt(p), z=B^T x, a=z/||z||. q_diag_canonical(i)=sum_h B_ih^2 a_h^2. The constant direction makes ||z||>0 for any normalized nonnegative p.
canonical_diagonal.evaluation: Use the exact formula with certified square-root/sum/division intervals; round each probability uniquely to binary64. Apply the same label map and recorded loss routines as other rules; retain the existing mass/negative-probability gates. Do not clip, rotate or select this law by loss.
canonical_diagonal.library_invariance_scope: Conditional on identical emitted input bytes, state order and specified numerical-dependence rule. The exact rational directions and their normalized/sign-selected real values are unique; certified final rounding is unique. Does not assert that different spectral libraries emit the same vectors, or that rotating the input emitted vectors leaves the canonical rule unchanged.

infrastructure_precedence: SPEC_MISMATCH / BLOCKED_RUNTIME -> INCONCLUSIVE, no scientific verdict
INCOMPLETE_ACQUISITION / COMMITMENT_FAILURE -> INCONCLUSIVE, no scientific verdict
outcomes.contrast_pass: Standalone endpoint: applicable controls valid, support and interval/tail defined; lower simultaneous bound > margin, positive-benefit Holm p<=0.05, and all required named sensitivities evaluable with no strict sign reversal. Contrast pair PASS requires both maps. Competitor margin zero; cross-term margin 1/240.
outcomes.contrast_fail: Validated endpoint upper simultaneous bound <= margin establishes exclusion of the registered advantage, independently of p; upper<0 additionally establishes adverse direction. Keep such a local failure visible even if another endpoint is unresolved. Control-invalid values cannot establish failure.
outcomes.contrast_neutral: Complete interval evidence neither passing nor excluding advantage (including lower>margin but Holm p>0.05) is an inconclusive endpoint, not an established FAIL.
outcomes.serviceability: Pass per map iff S_2 upper<=0 with applicable controls/evidence/sensitivities valid; fail if S_2 lower>0; otherwise inconclusive. Retain -S_2 primary benefit tail in fixed Holm family without reversing printed S_2 signs.

joint_flag_definitions.control_failure: C: any required endpoint has a positively failed applicable control. A missing/undecidable certificate is U rather than C. Descriptive-only O failures are excluded.
joint_flag_definitions.unresolved_evidence: U: any required endpoint or sensitivity missing, numerical-unresolved, vacuous, non-evaluable or neutral/inconclusive by interval/p criteria. Preserve all valid local pass/fail annotations.
joint_flag_definitions.named_sensitivity_reversal: R: any inherited required named point/deletion atom strictly reverses its endpoint's unrounded primary sign; zeros and bootstrap replicate signs do not count. Random-orientation signs never count.
joint_flag_definitions.established_endpoint_failure: F: at least one required validated endpoint has the exclusion/failure gate above; cannot be manufactured from invalid control evidence.

outcomes.decision_table_scope: The same exhaustive sixteen-row table applies separately to competitor-family and cross-term joint verdicts after infrastructure checks. C then U then R dominates F. No row silently ignores an established local failure; publish all flags and per-endpoint statuses. In the all-false row PASS requires all local pass predicates, otherwise neutral evidence is U and INCONCLUSIVE.
outcomes.competitor_joint_required: 11 competitor advantages on both maps plus serviceability on both maps. This family result is ancillary to the single canonical corrective headline.
outcomes.cross_term_joint_required: canonical advantage at 1/240 on both maps only. No oracle, random orientation or historical SVD endpoint is required.

all 11 advantages plus serviceability on raw and package

endpoint_control_dependencies.scope: Own descriptive validity only; O failures or orientation sign differences never veto a primary endpoint; shared I/A/F/C failure may also affect primary endpoints through their own dependencies.

explicit_cases: canonical pair PASS plus a failed/incomplete descriptive orientation report -> canonical joint PASS if its own dependencies pass; descriptive report unavailable, no oracle endpoint exists
canonical validated FAIL plus descriptive report incomplete -> FAIL if all primary evidence/controls/sensitivities complete; otherwise retain local FAIL and apply C/U/R precedence
one map unresolved and the other validated upper<=margin -> INCONCLUSIVE_UNRESOLVED with the other map exclusion prominently retained
shared span/full-law control failure -> INCONCLUSIVE_CONTROL_FAILURE for every dependent endpoint, never a favorable or adverse scientific verdict
canonical-only certificate failure leaves non-diagonal standalone endpoints computable under fixed family adjustment, but both required canonical joint results inconclusive
orientation-only control failure -> report affected descriptive slots/reference unavailable; no effect on primary gates
no exclusion but Holm non-rejection or straddling bound -> INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS
any inherited named sensitivity reversal -> no joint PASS even with otherwise favorable intervals; an orientation-report sign variation has no such effect
outcomes.paper_policy: No paper change until authorized fresh execution and independent review. Supersede historical diagonal evidence used for the corrected headline, not the truth of the historical computations. Preserve v21/v24 and competitor diagonal artifacts, historical-stack reproduction and original family adjustments; other historical comparators retain their scope. Chronology records original registrations, basis ambiguity discovery, historical reproduction, corrective freeze, fresh acquisition and all reviewed outcomes.

orientation_sensitivity.role: Prospectively fixed descriptive report; no p-values, confidence intervals, tests, optimization, inferential families or verdict dependencies. These rotations are never used to choose a comparator or membership.
orientation_sensitivity.justification: 128 independent per-unit rotations provide a fixed exploratory empirical distribution at manageable rank-two-through-six cost. Its order-statistic resolution is 1/128; this is neither exhaustive orientation coverage nor a precision/power guarantee. No expansion or early stopping after looking at contrasts.
orientation_sensitivity.scope: Each evaluation uses its own unchanged primary admitted unit cohort. All ranks are included. All 128 report slots are scheduled before scoring; the same slot index k aggregates independent per-unit draws, not one shared rotation across differing spans.
orientation_sensitivity.orbit: For each unit canonical ideal B and normalized a, q_R(i)=sum_h (BR)_ih^2 (R^T a)_h^2, R in O(r). Random rotations may rotate the constant axis; they do not preserve the constant-first canonical basis.

seeds.meaning: Domain-only seed constants for orientation streams, not runner seeds or replacement acquisitions.

orientation_sensitivity.identity: Complete unit identity is the JSON array [experiment, configuration label, acquisition seed, internal context identity, resolution k, recorded step] in unchanged collection order. Encode as UTF-8 sorted-key compact JSON with no newline; include exact restricted-input SHA256 separately. Collision/duplicate identities fail the report.
draw_algorithm: For each unit and zero-based k=0,...,127, create an independent SHA256/RNGStream with the frozen orientation domain below. No NumPy global RNG and no runner/sample RNG are consumed.

Draw r*r independent standard normal entries in row-major order using Box-Muller pairs. Each open uniform is ((word >> 12)+0.5)/2^52, exactly binary64 in (0,1). For u,v use z0=sqrt(-2 log u) cos(2*pi*v), z1=sqrt(-2 log u) sin(2*pi*v), Python math in that operation order with math.pi; keep both outputs in order and discard the unused second normal only when r*r is odd. Apply the pinned libm/runtime.

Use numpy.linalg.qr(G, mode=reduced), under the registered numerical worker. For each j multiply Q column j by +1 if R_jj>0, else -1 if R_jj<0. Do not impose determinant +1. This is Haar on O(r) for ideal independent Gaussian inputs; finite-word normals and floating QR approximate that law, and the finite algorithm and actual matrix bytes are the reproducibility contract.

If a diagonal pivot is zero or any output nonfinite, advance attempt=0,...,7 in the domain and regenerate the whole matrix. After eight failed attempts retain that slot as descriptive-unresolved. Never choose an orientation by its score.

Serialize normal bytes, Q/R bytes, sign vector, attempt, stream counters and input/runtime hashes. Evaluate q_R in a fixed scalar binary64 sequence: round ideal canonical B entries once by the canonical certificates; compute z=B^T sqrt(p) and normalize in ascending state/column order with math.fsum; b=B R and a_R=R^T a with ascending index math.fsum; q_R(i)=math.fsum(b_ih*b_ih*a_R_h*a_R_h) in ascending h. Retain inherited law mass/negative gates; do not claim these descriptive laws have certified exact rounding.
orientation_sensitivity.historical_stack_svd: One additional descriptive law per unit, using the inherited _oriented_basis under the pinned historical NumPy 2.5.2 / OpenBLAS 0.3.34.0.0 stack and its original q_diag operation sequence. Compute only on fresh v25 captures; it is neither a primary competitor nor a Holm member. Serialize basis, singular values, prediction and stack identity.
orientation_sensitivity.scoring: For raw and package, use the same fresh endpoints and primary TV loss. For each random slot k form D_f,k=ell_f(q_R_k)-ell_f(q_full) with the same equal-weight hierarchy and source-half weights. Apply each evaluation's inherited tie/zeroing convention at the original grain. Also persist unzeroed unit contrasts for description. Historical SVD contrast uses the identical cohort and aggregation. Brier orientation scoring is not registered.
report: all per-unit random and historical-SVD TV contrasts and draw/commit records
all 128 aggregate D_f,k for each map/evaluation, in k order
empirical min, Hyndman-Fan type-7 Q1/median/Q3, max, mean, and counts at/below zero and 1/240 of the 128 complete aggregate values
canonical aggregate and historical-SVD aggregate as separately labeled reference points, not included in random-orientation quantiles
orientation_sensitivity.incompleteness: A missing/failed unit for a slot makes that whole aggregate slot undefined: no changing denominator or recomputing on a convenient subset. Publish slot count and all reasons. Publish quantiles only when all 128 slots are complete; otherwise publish complete slot values but mark distribution summary unavailable. A historical SVD failure affects only that reference. A sensitivity-report-only failure or sign variation does not block, fail or rescue any primary verdict.

freeze: The freeze is the git commit of the specification and the code.
